examples.question_text: A nursery plants $80$ trays, each containing $16$ seeds. Each seed germinates independently with probability $0.7$. The number of trays containing exactly $12$ germinating seeds is recorded. Identify $n$, $p$, $N$ and $r$.
examples.solution_text:
One experiment is one tray. Success means a seed germinates.
$n=16$, $p=0.7$, $N=80$, $r=12$.

examples.question_text:
A grower plants $70$ trays, each containing $18$ seedlings. Each seedling survives independently with probability $0.8$.
(a) Find the expected number of surviving seedlings in one tray.
(b) Find the expected total number of surviving seedlings across all $70$ trays.
examples.solution_text:
Let $X$ count surviving seedlings in one tray, so $X\sim\text{Bin}(18,0.8)$.
(a) $\begin{aligned}E(X)&=np\\&=18(0.8)\\&=14.4\end{aligned}$
The expected number is $14.4$ seedlings per tray.
(b) $\begin{aligned}70E(X)&=70(14.4)\\&=1008\end{aligned}$
The expected total is $1008$ surviving seedlings.

examples.question_text: A laboratory tests $240$ dishes, each containing $6$ seeds. Each seed fails to germinate independently with probability $0.2$. Find the expected number of dishes containing exactly $2$ failed seeds, to the nearest dish.
examples.solution_text:
Success means a seed fails to germinate. Let $X$ count failed seeds in one dish.
$X\sim\text{Bin}(6,0.2)$, $N=240$, $r=2$.
$\begin{aligned}P(X=2)&={}^{6}C_{2}(0.2)^2(0.8)^4\\&=0.24576\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}NP(X=2)&=240(0.24576)\\&=58.9824\end{aligned}$
Approximately $59$ dishes are expected to contain exactly $2$ failed seeds.

examples.question_text: A packing shed checks $200$ boxes, each containing $5$ fruit. Each fruit is bruised independently with probability $0.2$. Find the expected number of boxes containing at most $1$ bruised fruit, to the nearest box.
examples.solution_text:
Let $X$ count bruised fruit in one box, so $X\sim\text{Bin}(5,0.2)$ and $N=200$.
At most $1$ means $X=0$ or $X=1$.
$\begin{aligned}P(X\leq1)&=P(X=0)+P(X=1)\\&=(0.8)^5+{}^{5}C_{1}(0.2)(0.8)^4\\&=0.73728\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}NP(X\leq1)&=200(0.73728)\\&=147.456\end{aligned}$
Approximately $147$ boxes are expected to contain at most $1$ bruised fruit.

examples.question_text:
A nursery sells $320$ bundles, each containing $7$ cuttings. Each cutting wilts independently with probability $0.2$.
(a) Find the expected number of bundles containing at least $1$ wilted cutting.
(b) Find the expected number of bundles containing at least $2$ wilted cuttings.
Give each answer to the nearest bundle.
examples.solution_text:
Let $X$ count wilted cuttings in one bundle, so $X\sim\text{Bin}(7,0.2)$ and $N=320$.
(a) The complement of at least $1$ is $X=0$.
$\begin{aligned}P(X\geq1)&=1-P(X=0)\\&=1-(0.8)^7\\&=0.7902848\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}NP(X\geq1)&=320(0.7902848)\\&=252.891136\end{aligned}$
Approximately $253$ bundles.
(b) The complement of at least $2$ is $X=0$ or $X=1$.
$\begin{aligned}P(X\geq2)&=1-P(X=0)-P(X=1)\\&=1-(0.8)^7-{}^{7}C_{1}(0.2)(0.8)^6\\&=0.4232832\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}NP(X\geq2)&=320(0.4232832)\\&=135.450624\end{aligned}$
Approximately $135$ bundles.

examples.question_text: A grower plants $250$ pots, each containing $8$ seeds. Each seed germinates independently with probability $0.9$. Find the expected number of pots in which at most $6$ seeds germinate, to the nearest pot.
examples.solution_text:
Let $X$ count germinating seeds in one pot, so $X\sim\text{Bin}(8,0.9)$ and $N=250$.
The complement of at most $6$ is $X=7$ or $X=8$.
$\begin{aligned}P(X\leq6)&=1-P(X=7)-P(X=8)\\&=1-{}^{8}C_{7}(0.9)^7(0.1)-(0.9)^8\\&=0.18689527\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}NP(X\leq6)&=250(0.18689527)\\&=46.7238175\end{aligned}$
Approximately $47$ pots are expected to have at most $6$ germinating seeds.

E(X)=18×0.8=14.4 surviving seedlings per tray. Across 70 trays, the expected total is 70×14.4=1008. Both aligned blocks begin with complete equations; neither requires a phantom equals gutter.
P(X=2)=15×0.2²×0.8⁴=0.24576. Expected frequency=240×0.24576=58.9824, rounding to 59 dishes.
